impact: If a command forks a descendant that inherits stdout/stderr and the direct child exits, capture remains open until the deadline, but `terminate` sees the direct child has exited and skips `killpg`. The call raises a timeout while the descendant remains alive and can continue consuming resources or touching files. I read the full subprocess supervisor, grepped all production callers, and checked the direct-child timeout/interrupt tests; none provides outer cleanup or covers an exited leader with a live descendant. The trigger depends on an external command or configured git helper forking, so confidence is reduced.
title: [missing-subprocess-cleanup] If a command forks a descendant that inherits stdout/stderr and the direct child
